cross_references.note: CalVCB application and related administrative proceedings are 'official proceedings authorized by law' under §425.16(e)(1). Any tort claim arising from statements made in the CalVCB proceeding is subject to anti-SLAPP. §1094.5 is the vehicle to challenge the CalVCB denial; §425.16 is the shield against claims arising from the application itself.

Reports to OPD and other law enforcement are statements to official proceedings under §425.16(e)(1). A civil claim based on the content of a police report filed by the petitioner is subject to anti-SLAPP. The PC §148.5 criminal prosecution for false police report is the parallel criminal track; civil claims based on the same report face anti-SLAPP.

Statements made in family law proceedings (DVRO applications, custody hearings, declarations) are official proceeding statements under §425.16(e)(1). Counter-claims or tort claims based on the content of those statements face anti-SLAPP challenge. The family law proceeding context is exactly where SLAPP retaliation most commonly occurs.

CalVCB application statements are protected under §425.16(e)(2) — statements made in connection with issues under consideration by an official body. Any civil claim premised on the application's content is subject to anti-SLAPP.

DFEH/CRD complaints are official proceedings authorized by law under §425.16(e)(1). Civil claims premised on the content of those complaints (e.g., malicious prosecution after a FEHA charge) face anti-SLAPP challenge.
